correctness.rationale: Direct closed-neighborhood domination shows gamma(K_m x K_n)=3 for m,n>=4 and exactly two triple shapes: corner and three-row/three-column matching. Counts L=mn(m-1)(n-1), T=6 C(m,3)C(n,3); retained-pair completion yields degrees mn-1 and 3((m-2)(n-2)+1). Regular iff (m-3)(n-3)=1, i.e. 4x4. For any two triples their union occupies <=6 row/column labels; reducing to any of 25 p-by-q kernels with 2<=p,q<=6 is therefore exhaustive for arbitrary m,n. Independent bitset enumeration verified ALL 25 exact finite-kernel graphs, every source vertex reaches every other in <=3 jumps, largest 3300 states. Every intermediate corner/matching remains dominating in the original grid; two disjoint corner triples need >=3 jumps, proving diameter exactly three. Direct independent small-graph degree checks included 4x4=240 vertices/1800 edges, 4x5=480/4800, 6x6=3300/76950. The finite lemma is exhaustive under a rigorously bounded support reduction, not finite-to-infinite extrapolation.
